The reviews for the first laptop looked fine. Then Yara found a video about a second one, and a forum thread warning about a third. By the end of the first week there were twenty laptops in a spreadsheet, and every new page added a doubt.
"Does it get hot?" "Is the battery honest in the reviews?" Felix, who shared the flat, watched her scroll one evening. "It's been three weeks. Just pick one." "Then I'll read one more comparison." 
Her old laptop crashed during a group assignment, and Yara finished at the library, queuing for a free computer. The spreadsheet still had no winner.

qa.q: How many laptops did Yara have in the spreadsheet?
qa.a: Yara had twenty laptops in the spreadsheet.

qa.q: What was Yara feeling as each new review appeared?
qa.a: Yara felt doubt, since every new page added a worry instead of making the choice clearer.

qa.q: What different approach could Yara use to end the search?
qa.a: Yara could list the three things that matter most and pick the first laptop that meets them, since good enough would end the loop.

qa.q: How does Felix see the three weeks of reading?
qa.a: Felix has watched it for weeks and wants Yara to just pick one, seeing more reading as unlikely to help.

grounding: A student compares twenty laptops for weeks without deciding, and new information only adds doubt.

passage: In the engineering hostel common room, Chinmay had three browser windows open and a spreadsheet with twenty laptops. It was week three. Every night after dinner he read more reviews. One said the battery was great; the next said it died in two hours. One liked the keyboard; another said it broke. He kept adding columns: weight, ports, fan noise. His roommate Tushar leaned over. "You needed one for coding, right? Any of the top five would do." "But what if there's a better one?" Chinmay said, and opened another review. Meanwhile his old laptop crashed during a lab submission, and he had to borrow Tushar's. The spreadsheet had grown to fourteen columns. He was no closer to choosing, and more confused than when he started.

qa.q: How many laptops were in Chinmay's spreadsheet?
What was Chinmay feeling after three weeks of reviews?
qa.a: He felt more doubtful and confused than when he started, afraid of missing a better choice.

qa.q: What other approach could work for Chinmay?
qa.a: Pick the few features he really needs for coding, set a deadline, and choose the first laptop that meets them, as Tushar suggested.

qa.q: How is Tushar affected by Chinmay's endless comparing?
qa.a: Tushar ends up lending his own laptop and probably feels a little exasperated watching the spreadsheet grow.

grounding: A student compares twenty laptops for three weeks and still can't choose, with each new review adding doubt.
